projects.name: Solar + Energy Storage on Garage
projects.description: Install 5-7 solar panels on south-facing garage roof face (20x12 ft, ~2-2.8 kW) plus battery storage. Solar = standalone ROI investment (~5yr payback at $0.42/kWh). Battery = generator alternative (no lot space for generator). 30% federal ITC applies to both when paired.
projects.notes: DESIGN: South garage face only. 5 portrait panels = 2.0 kW; 7 mixed = 2.8 kW. ~3,200-4,500 kWh/yr production (20-26% offset). All-in after ITC: solar ~$9-10k, battery ~$9-10k. VENDORS: Sunergy (sunergy.com) — EnergySage 2026 CA Installer of Year, Enphase Platinum, no door-to-door. NRG Clean Power (nrgcleanpower.com) — Diamond Certified, 35yr, San Mateo County, 40yr warranty. Tesla Energy (tesla.com/energy) — online only. AVOID: Sunrun.

tasks.title: Analyze energy usage and size system
tasks.notes: 17,178 kWh/yr at $0.42/kWh avg. Target: 5-7 panels south garage face (20x12 ft) = 2-2.8 kW. ~5yr payback after ITC.

tasks.title: Research and shortlist solar installers
tasks.notes: Shortlist: Sunergy (sunergy.com, Enphase Platinum, no door-to-door), NRG Clean Power (nrgcleanpower.com, Diamond Certified, San Mateo County), Tesla Energy (tesla.com/energy, online only). Avoid Sunrun.

tasks.title: Contact installers for quotes
tasks.notes: Spec: south garage face (20x12 ft, 5-7 panels, ~2-2.8 kW), paired battery (Enphase IQ or Powerwall 3), detached garage sub-panel interconnect. Ask each for: $/W, panel brand, inverter type, battery spec, warranty, timeline, ITC total. Request free shade/LIDAR analysis.

tasks.title: Compare quotes and select installer
tasks.notes: Prefer Enphase microinverters over string inverter. Compare $/W, battery spec, warranty, timeline. 30% ITC on full system incl. battery.

tasks.title: Confirm ITC timing — credit files in year PTO is granted
tasks.notes: 30% federal ITC on Form 5695. Claimed in tax year Permission to Operate granted by PG&E. Battery qualifies only when solar-paired. Plan install timing accordingly.

insights.summary: The sustained high device count (22-24) paired with zero camera activity over four hours suggests the family is likely gathered in a camera-blind zone (e.g., backyard or garage) or the cameras may be offline; a quick status check is recommended to ensure monitoring is active.

The combination of a sustained ~21-23 mobile device count with zero camera activity over a 4-hour Friday morning strongly indicates the presence sensor is misclassifying IoT/smart home devices as mobile phones rather than tracking actual occupancy. This matters because it can corrupt occupancy analytics and trigger incorrect home automations.

The sustained high and rapidly fluctuating device count (21–26) paired with zero camera activity indicates network polling artifacts or stationary IoT devices rather than active human presence. A routine network health check is recommended to prevent false presence triggers and optimize Wi-Fi performance.

The network's connected mobile device count jumped from 25 to 27 in the last two minutes, suggesting unexpected guests or a delivery may have just arrived, especially given the Friday morning timeframe and lack of corresponding camera activity.

The steady rise in connected devices (22→26) alongside zero camera motion and confirmed sleep metrics indicates a normal late-night settling pattern, with the 02:24 device addition likely being a routine phone check or IoT reconnect rather than an intrusion.

The sustained 20–25 device count combined with zero camera motion and late-night timing indicates the family is settled in bedrooms or private rooms outside camera view, with the high count likely inflated by smart home IoT devices or personal electronics charging. This forms a coherent late-night routine pattern rather than a security concern.

The sustained 20–25 device count paired with zero camera motion at 11:25 PM strongly suggests either the cameras are offline or all occupants (including Miller’s guests) have settled down for the night with motion detection disabled. This matters because it creates a monitoring blind spot that could mask late-night activity or security events.

The combination of 20+ active devices, zero camera motion, and the Thursday 10:23 PM timestamp strongly indicates Miller’s friends are gathered in a single, darkened room where motion sensors don’t trigger, but the late hour suggests Steve may want to verify they’re winding down.

The sustained 20+ device count paired with zero camera motion for four hours strongly suggests either a concentrated gathering in a camera-blind zone (like a basement or garage) or a network/IoT device count anomaly rather than normal household movement. This warrants a quick verification to ensure the kids' gathering is safe and supervised, or to rule out a smart home network glitch.

The persistent 20–23 device count with zero camera motion suggests either Miller’s friends are over in a single room with lights off, or a network glitch is inflating presence data. Steve should quickly verify occupancy or check the router to rule out phantom connections.
